newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM plays down share buy-back reports.
newsitem.headline: KLM plays down share buy-back reports.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV on Tuesday played down market speculation it was poised to buy back its own shares, saying it was assessing options to reduce its cash position.
"KLM is looking at a number of options for its ample cash reserves, but no decision has been taken as yet," spokesman Hans Leijte said.
Dealers said earlier KLM might be about to launch a share buy-back to better utilize its excess cash.
But Leijte said the airline was still considering what action to take.

"There are various possibilities: we could accelerate debt repayments, invest in high-yielding aviation-related activities or buy back a portion of our own shares," he said, adding "no firm decisions have yet emerged from what we said in August would be a long review process."

The possibility of a share buy-back was first raised at the publication of KLM's 1996/97 first-quarter results in August, when the Dutch carrier said the sale of preference shares in U.S. partner Northwest Airlines had generated a book profit of 179 million guilders.
KLM shares were trading up 1.10 guilders at 43.30 around 1225 GMT on a buoyant Amsterdam bourse, off the day's high of 43.50.
The carrier is due to unveil first-half results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 1997 on November 5.
The company's March 31, 1996 balance sheet showed a cash position of 2.63 billion guilders and total assets of 16.5 billion.
